newsitem.title: USA: Jews said put in Swiss forced labor camps.
newsitem.headline: Jews said put in Swiss forced labor camps.

text.p: FBI director J. Edgar Hoover warned the U.S. State Department in 1942 that the Swiss were putting male Jewish refugees into forced labour camps, a secret memorandum obtained by the World Jewish Congress and released on Monday said.

In the memo to Assistant Secretary of State Adolf Berle Jr. dated May 15, 1942, Hoover said secret informants had told him that the position of the refugees was becoming "more and more difficult" and that Swiss Jewish organisations lacked the funds to support them.
Hoover headed the FBI from 1924 until his death in 1972.
The Swiss made Jewish groups pay for the upkeep of Jewish refugees during the war, while the government paid for the upkeep of other groups.
Switzerland barred thousands of Jews who had sought refuge in the neutral nation but several thousand did manage to get through.
According to Hoover, Jewish men between the ages of 18 and 45 were most often put to work doing farm work and road projects.
Hoover added in the memo that Jewish refugees were denied access to gainful occupations.
